And there is nothing controversial about that that they maintained law and order, because law and order needs to be maintained for all citizen: Serbs, Siptars, Romas, everybody. That is general interest and that is probably the way the commander understood it as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Very well, if we could see 6D1470. If I can just have a moment's indulgence. I think it may be P896. I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, this is an order from the Pristina military district from the 27th of March, 1999. And let's start by looking at Tasks under number 2 at the bottom of the page. You can look at the first two items. Very first thing it says, sir - and we'll go on to look at the next page in a moment - the first thing it says is: "To protect the Serbian population." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Then underneath that it says: "To guard roads, military installations, and other features." Do you see that as well?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And one would think, sir, that in order to guard roads, might also involve the use of roadblocks, might it not?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is that your question? May I answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is my answer to that question: First of all, this is a document, as you can see it as well, was not written by me. I cannot see the signature down here. Could you please tell me who signed this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Let's actually look to the second page, sir, and we can actually go through the document in more order. Perhaps we can jump to the last page so you can see the signature. It's Colonel Pesic.

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it. I see it. I understand. That is the commander of the Pristina military district Colonel Zlatomir Pesic. So it is his document. In relation to this, I can just tell you what my opinion is, otherwise, I cannot interpret what it was that the commander -- very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I want to give you a chance to look at the document in a bit more detail, I think that's fair.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: If we could look at page 3.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: It's at number 5.4. You can read that, sir, but I'll read it in English as well, it says: "The 50th Military Territorial District shall guard military facilities in Pristina and in co-ordination with forces of the MUP and internal security shall protect features of importance (hospitals, post offices, TV, and radio stations)." And it also says: "It shall protect the Serbian population in the southern part of the town of Pristina." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So here the 50th Military Territorial Detachment is tasked not only with guarding facilities in Pristina but with protecting the Serbian population in the southern part of Pristina, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see what is written there, and I hear what I hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, these are just a couple of the orders that we have in our possession. But in fact, I put to you that as of the end of February of 1999, the VJ had already begun deploying large numbers of tanks, APCs, and troops surrounding Pristina; do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not agree with that. And it's not correct. It's not a question of me disagreeing or not agreeing, it is simply not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, you have testified yourself that there were many KLA attacks after the war started, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were many attacks.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And one would think that with KLA attacks taking place in and on Pristina generally, and given the taskings, just the two taskings you've already seen, that the VJ would need to be ready to respond, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The VJ was ready to respond, and it was supposed to respond. The problem is that in many such terrorist attacks neither the army nor the police responded. You may recall that I told you when Colonel Nikolic was wounded and when the composites got killed and four policemen were killed in one and three policemen were wounded in another neighbourhood in Pristina and the police did not kill a single terrorist when all of that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: But the problem, sir, is that it's not just that you said that they didn't respond. It's that you were clear and you repeatedly said that there was not a single combat unit there, and that's obviously not the case.

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said what I said, and I stand by it. It depends on who means what under the term "combat unit." You know that in relation to that, what is not combat is sometimes combat. I know full well on the basis of the doctrine of our army and law and regulations what combat units are. Somebody else does not understand it that way. Just like there is the problem of excessive use of force. Some people assess it in one way and others assess it in another way. Some people assess excessive use of force when a single machine-gun is used; whereas, others do not consider excessive use of force even when you use an atomic bomb. So from the point of view of our doctrine in Pristina, there was not a single combat unit, and that is what I stand by.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I think we have your position, sir. Let's move on. You testified very directly again, sir, in the Milutinovic case that there was no destruction of Albanian religious buildings. You repeated that again today. No destruction of Albanian religious buildings, certainly no destruction of mosques. Do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. And indeed there was no destruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can we see P01136, please. Page 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: The building depicted here, sir, on the screen, that's the Emperor's Mosque, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the Emperor's Mosque. It's probably the Emperor's Mosque. There were discussions as to which mosque this was, if it's near the high school Ivo Lola Ribar and near the watch-tower in Pristina then it is the Emperor's Mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And, in fact, sir, you went to high school 10 metres away from that mosque on that site, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if that's it, I saw it all the time. Before the aggression, and during the aggression. I had occasion to see it many times and to participate in securing it from Siptar terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: It was also close to your command post, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Now, sir, you did identify this mosque in the Milutinovic case and you at that time were also able to describe it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: If we look at D712.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: If we can see page 116, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: At line 18, you said: "As for the right-hand part of the picture where the flames are, that's not the mosque." And Judge Bonomy asked you: "Well, is it the historical archive of the Islamic community?" And you responded: "Possibly. That's where a similar building was, and close to it is Sahat Kula, the watch-tower." And you pointed out that that adjoining building wasn't the mosque. And Judge Bonomy then asks you --

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Actually if we can go to the next page at the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: He asks you: "Can you not say whether this was the Islamic community's historical archive?" Your answer was that you weren't sure precisely whether that was the archive but you knew the building very well. Do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And you've obviously seen from that photograph, sir, that the building was engulfed in flames, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the picture you can see flames.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So it would appear, sir, that your claim that not a single house of worship or religious building was either damaged or destroyed was in fact not correct, do you agree?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I disagree with you. Quite fully. That is absolutely not true. And please allow me to explain why it is not true. If you allow me then I may start now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: You may explain, sir, but please if you can, keep your answer concise.

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll do my best to be very brief, and I'm sure that I will keep my answer shorter than your question. I asked Judge Bonomy then when that building was set on fire. And he said, and you can read it there, that that was on the 15th of June. I said that I was in Pristina then as well, and that I did not notice that. If it was on the 15th of June, then it is certain that it wasn't set on fire by the members of the police or the members of the VJ. Then I went on to say that that mosque, the Emperor's Mosque at that time just like the mosque near my command post, this one was nearby as well, it was secured by English KFOR troops who entered it then. They put sand bags in front of all the mosques and guarded them with weapons. And I said that they took such good care of it that even a car of a friend of mine, Dragan Lazic, that was parked right in front of the their eyes and Siptar terrorists stole that car. Well, that is exactly how they protected that mosque from the Siptar terrorists. It is possible that they did it together and they allowed it to be set on fire. The army and the police would never have allowed that kind of thing to happen. While we were providing security there, not a single place of worship was destroyed, and I continue to stand by that that during the aggression not a single Islamic place of worship in the town of Pristina was damaged or destroyed, and that is the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, I see that now you seem to be acknowledging that this mosque was damaged or destroyed, or certainly the adjoining building was destroyed. But that's not even what you said before. Maybe that you are trying to --

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The mosque was not destroyed. And none of what I said is in dispute. After the English KFOR troops entered, then it was under them that this mosque was set on fire, if it was set on fire at all. I said that I did not see it. If that did happen, it happened only when the English KFOR forces entered. After the entrance -- entry of the English KFOR troops, the entire provincial library in the centre of Pristina was set on fire for days it was ablaze, and all of the citizens of Pristina saw that the library was burning for days, and all of this while English KFOR was providing security. Now, that's the truth, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: There's a couple of problems with that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I see my friend is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I waited for the witness to complete his answer. It seems to me that my learned friend, Mr. Behar, is making assertions that cannot be derived from the witness's answer. The witness said that he never saw the mosque that is in the picture on fire. And I think that that can be seen in the transcript as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, the problem is that it's not that you said that the Serb forces didn't destroy any mosques, it's that you said generally as regards the city of Pristina, I can say not a single house of worship or religious building was either damaged or destroyed. So even if you had, in fact, believed that somehow it was a co-operation between -- [Overlapping speakers] ... and the Albanians, you said, sir, that not a single house of worship or religious building was damaged or destroyed, and that's not the case, is it?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree with you. I said that, namely, that not a single mosque or any Islamic place of worship in the territory of Pristina was destroyed or damaged during the aggression. I hope that you know until when the aggression lasted. It was up until the Kumanovo agreement. This building that is next door to the mosque, so it's not the mosque itself, I didn't see when that was set on fire either. But it was probably set on fire and if it was, it was after the English KFOR entered Pristina. There is not any information to the effect that they killed a single terrorist, whereas in the centre of Pristina, English KFOR killed a few Serb civilians who were just walking by. They killed a few innocent civilians. In front of the theatre, they killed an innocent civilian who was just walking there, and there was blood all over in the street. They didn't even kill or do anything to the terrorists that then set this mosque on fire. Nothing. Now, that is the truth, sir. The army or the police had no powers there whatsoever. Had we had authority there then, the mosque would not have been set on fire, if it had been set on fire, but that is something that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I think we have your position, sir. Sir, when you testified in the Milutinovic case you used the term "Siptar" repeatedly to refer to the Kosovo Albanians, and you, in fact, did so throughout your testimony. Do you recall that having done so you then engaged in a relatively lengthy exchange with the Chamber over the question of whether the term had a derogatory or an inappropriate connotation?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall having discussed that. There's no doubt about that. In relation to that question, I see nothing in dispute. One uses that term to describe most of the population at that time in Kosovo. You saw hundreds and thousands of documents before this Tribunal where you could see that even my command and Supreme Command used the same term. I see no reason for me to do otherwise, especially because it is not derogatory and especially in view of the fact that the very population living there call themselves that. I always took into full account every single person living in that territory. I never distinguished between them on the grounds of religion or ethnicity, the then-constitution of the FRY and Articles 43 and 45 --

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: That's fine, we don't need to get into the constitution.

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I noticed again, sir, you use the term "Siptar" repeatedly on Wednesday to refer to Kosovo Albanian civilians. I think you have been quite clear then in your position that neither then nor now do you see anything wrong with you using that term; is that fair?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct, I use that term. It is true that I use that term because that population calls themselves that. In the waiting room, just before I entered the courtroom, I saw that a part of Albania has the same name, so even at this Tribunal there is such a word, "Siptar." I don't see what the question is here. It's not derogatory whatsoever. I don't know where you get this idea that it is. I use that word with deep respect for the population that calls itself that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Let's go step by step then, sir. First the Serb word for an Albanian is Albanac or Albanci, correct? I see you're nodding, if you can just verbalise, are you saying yes?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say what you want me to. I can tell you what I think is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Just yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Therefore, this is your answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: That's fine. Sir, I don't need a long explanation. I just actually asked you that, I saw you nodding your head, but because we have a transcript here, we actually need to write down an answer yes or no. So do I take it your answer since you were nodding was yes, and I can move to the next question?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say yes. I didn't say no either. Please put your question and listen to my answer. I'll briefly provide you with one. I think that's only fair.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So let me ask again, sir. Is the Serb word for an Albanian Albanac or in plural Albanci; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's no problem about the words "Albanci" or "Siptar." Serbs call the inhabitants of Albania the way they call themselves. In the area of Kosovo and Metohija, Serbs call the Siptar population as the population calls itself. I've explained already that I have nothing against what they call themselves. This is what they call themselves. It's in their dictionaries, in their documents. I don't see what the dispute is. There's no pejorative or derogatory connotations to it. If it is in any way related or disputed concerning the aggression or terrorism, well, then I don't see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Behar, I think you can take it that the answer to your question was yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And, sir, if I can cut right to the point then, let me just suggest it to you as directly as I can. I'm going to suggest to you, sir, that the word "Siptar" when used in the Serbian language by a Serb person speaking Serbian, assumes a very negative connotation and that specifically, sir, it has a cultural connotation of referring to someone as a second-rank citizen. Is that something, sir, that you are aware of because I might have thought that having grown up in Pristina you would be well aware of that connotation?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not true. I'm amazed that you came to that conclusion. It is incorrect. Why would that mean that they were second rate? People I worked with always believed Siptars and other people were fully equal in every aspect. This is what we abided by in our daily work and practice. I have many friends among Albanians in Pristina and Kosovo and further afield. I'll always have such friends, and I'll always like them irrespective of what they are called. If they call themselves Albanians, I will call them so. If they call themselves Siptar, I will call them that way. That's my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: That's fine, sir. And to be clear, I wasn't asking if you had Albanian friends, I was asking about the term. Sir, are you familiar with Zoran Andjelkovic? Do you know who he is?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. I know who Zoran Andjelkovic is. And I know what his role was during the aggression.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And he was, in fact, a president of the temporary Executive Council for Kosovo-Metohija, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he also commanded the civilian protection of Kosovo and Metohija. He had his own Chief of Staff, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: If we can see Defence 65 ter 1673, please. I'll need page 58. I think, if it assists, it's D010-3011. Page 58, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, this is Mr. Andjelkovic's testimony from the Milutinovic trial, that's the same trial that you testified in. He will again be a witness in this trial. And I'll read out part of this to you, sir, but the context is that Mr. Andjelkovic is taking great issue and great offence to the suggestion that as a Serb he might have referred to the Albanians as Siptars. And if we look at line 4, he states: "Whenever I called the Albanians Siptars, all those who know me, both Albanians and Serbs, know that I would never say anything like that. I had a member of the temporary Executive Council replaced because he did not agree with me that Albanians and Turks and so on and so forth should be called members of ethnic communities, not even ethnic minorities, and there's this insinuation being made in these documents to the effect that I called the Albanians Siptars." He goes on, sir, to say: "This is just not true, this is an outrage both against me and against my Albanian friends, people that I still see on a regular basis." And then if we look down at line 23, just in case that wasn't clear enough, Judge Bonomy asks: "Are you saying that for you to refer to an Albanian by the use of the word "Siptar" is offensive?" And he states: "Yes, in my opinion." And he, in fact, continues to go on about how that term is derogatory, sir, but I won't take you through all of it. Having seen that, sir, do you recognise that the term "Siptar" as used in Serbian is derogatory?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I answer now?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A moment ago you heard me what I said, and I stand by it. I also stand by what I said in the Milutinovic case. As for what Mr. Andjelkovic said, there's no need for me to comment on it. That's his opinion, and there's really no need for me to comment. I stand by what I said. I don't want to change my testimony in that respect. I'm deeply convinced that what I said is true. This is what I felt, this is what I still think, and I think it is correct. In any case, you know people change statements, testimonies. Those same Siptars hold me in much higher regard, I believe, than they do Mr. Andjelkovic, but that's also a hypothesis of mine. He is quite a newcomer. He shared much less of their good or bad faith with them than I ever did. So much for Mr. Andjelkovic and his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Well, sir, I understand your point, you seem to be reiterating that you believe that this term is not offensive. And we've dealt with that. But even putting that aside, sir, surely if Kosovo Albanians are offended by your use of that term, then the term is offensive, do you agree?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if one wants to insult them or themselves, but what if they are not exchanging insults? When I was there, when I spoke with them and when I was exposed to NATO bombing, they were never insulted by that. I associated with them. I shared good and evil with them. And they were never insulted. And I was never insulted on their part. I did tell them if they wanted me to call them anything else, I could do so if they found that of their liking. Why not? And why would I have to change my previous conduct? I would still be doing that if I were down there. As for how they feel after the aggression and whether this is now an insult or not is something I don't know. I'm now completely outside that area. I have no knowledge of their feelings nowadays.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Just before we move on, sir, I'm not sure I understood part of what you had said earlier. You said that the -- some Siptars hold you in a higher regard and that they don't hold Mr. Andjelkovic in a high regard. Can you explain that? Why don't they hold Mr. Andjelkovic in a high regard?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think they don't hold him in any regard, but I just said that I believe they think better of me than of him for the simple reason because he spent shorter time with them than I did. He didn't share as much good and evil with them than I did. He only lived there for a short while before the aggression and after the aggression. Secondly, I make a distinction between myself and Mr. Andjelkovic on several levels. First and foremost, I am a soldier who hails from that area whereas he is a politician. You know that politicians have a different view of some things nowadays than they did before. I, however, cannot do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Okay, sir, let's try to keep this moving. Sir, you've made a number of observations and comments about the evidence of Nazalie Bala. I notice you discuss her evidence in some length again unprompted earlier today. I want to ask you some questions about the comments that you've made both in the Milutinovic trial and on Wednesday and here again today. First, sir, you have never been inside of Nazalie Bala's house, I take it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never been there, although I would like to. Even if I had been, there would have been nothing in dispute there. I did go down that street, and I think I know where her house is. Well, or I'm not actually sure whether I would be able to recognise her house or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Right. Just to focus again sir, you've never been inside her house, of course then you haven't been on her roof-top, correct? Where she says that she made these observations?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is absolutely correct. I have never been inside her house and especially not on her roof.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And, in fact, sir, you have told us, and I think this is clear from your previous testimony, you couldn't even recognise her house?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't really recognise her house because I had never seen it, but I can guess the location of it because I know Lapska Street quite well. And it's not too long of a street.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I know that you know the street, sir, and we'll come to that in a moment. But you've provided testimony, sir, detailed testimony to this Court that Ms. Bala could not possibly have seen what she saw from that roof-top, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She could not have seen it, what she says she did, from the roof of that house. And especially not the village of Kojlovica. As I said in the Milutinovic case, she would not have been able to see it even with a telescope, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Well, in fact, sir, she had binoculars. Let me take you through this step by step. First if we can look at your testimony in chief on Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And if we could see D717. Sorry, Your Honours, before I proceed, my colleague here observed that I hadn't tendered the transcript of Zoran Andjelkovic, which I took the witness through. I expect it will probably be tendered in the course of the Defence case, but I think in terms of good record-keeping it would probably be best to seek to tender it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: That was the exhibit, that was D010-3011.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01541.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, we are looking at the map that you marked on Wednesday, we can see where it's marked number 1 there, perhaps we could zoom in where it says number 1. But you, in fact, just identified a wide swathe of Ms. Bala's street on the map. And, in fact, that street which you can see from that is quite a long street, in fact, continues not just in the wide area that you circled but even on the other side of the cross street to the east. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So, in fact, sir, that street goes on for many a blocks, in fact, continues past a couple of major streets there, major intersections, and it's a fairly long street, would you agree?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree that it's a pretty long street. It's all relative. For example, look at Proatoska [phoen] Street, it is much longer than Lapska, then we have Gavrila Principa Street, much longer. This is one of the shorter ones. And as for the difference between short and long, it's a relative thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Would you agree, sir, the part of the street you've circled essentially a wide swathe of that street, do you agree? Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I circled it, I wasn't asked to circle the whole of it, but to circle a part of that street, and I did. And you can see clearly on the map how far it goes. Lapska Street is a whole street. And when Nazalie Bala was circling it, she didn't circle the whole street either, just a part of it. That's what I could read on that part of the map. That's not in dispute. Lapska Street is where it says it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I understand, sir. Let me see if I can be more specific. Sir, you've made a broad declaration that from this street, Lapska Street, that runs the whole distance that we can see in front of us, from that street, Ms. Bala could not possibly have seen any of the places that she described, correct? From nowhere along that street is what you've said.

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You asked me that a moment ago and I said that from Lapska Street, from her house and from her roof-top especially could not have been able to see the village of Kojlovica, not from her house and with the binoculars from the roof of her house.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, that's what you are saying now, but, in fact, it's already been made quite clear, I think, you don't know where her house is, you've never been inside it, you've never been on the roof. And what you've said repeatedly in your observations is that one couldn't see these places from that street, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said something that you are obviously trying to take note of. I said that it is in a flat area. I explained that in relation to the street's position and Vranjevac, it is in a flat area. That's not in dispute. Is there a problem for anyone to go to Pristina to get up on the roof and see whether Kojlovica can be seen or not, and that person can tell you that and then you can call me to task about my testimony. Someone goes there, takes a look, if you can see it you know. Milutin Filipovic was not telling the truth as a witness. If you can -- if you can't see it, then he was telling the truth. Why waste time? Although, I'm more than ready to co-operate with you on that. Let's take as much time as you have on your hands, and I'll give you my time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: But, sir, the problem is, and let me put this to you again because I'm not sure that I'm getting an answer to it, you don't know where the house is but you've been very certain in your claims, your repeated claims in the Milutinovic case and again here in the Djordjevic case, that she could not have seen the things she saw. But what I'm saying to you, sir, is that you do not know where on that street, and you have not known where on that street her house even is; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not. Her house is determined or its location was determined precisely. Her street is not just anywhere along Lapska Street, it is at number 30 and nowhere else. It is in Lapska Street and only there. From that street, from that house, one cannot see Kojlovica. I was in Kojlovica 40 years ago, 30 years ago, on the eve of the aggression, and I know where it is. I couldn't see that part of Pristina from Kojlovica, and I could not see Kojlovica from Lapska Street. Also, I couldn't see the house where he she lived in. 40 years ago my teacher in Kojlovica, Angelina Saranovic in Nusiceva Street, Number 7, in Belgrade, I used to go to see her and I would see her at school in Kojlovica, so you cannot see it. We should go to Nazalie Bala's house. Let's take a pair of binoculars, let's see if we can see Kojlovica or not. Let's clear that up once and for all. If you can see it, I'm wrong. If you can't, I'm right --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... understands the answer to be that from nowhere in the street can that village be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Sir, we are becoming impatient with your answers. You do not seem capable of giving a short answer to a question. If you listen to the answer, you can answer shortly. You are spending a very great deal of time talking about matters that have nothing to do with this case. That is not helping us to hear and understand what you want to say. Please carry on, Mr. Behar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, I see that you have again tried to assert or now, in fact, for the first time have tried to assert that you knew where her specific house was and I see that you know it's number 30 no doubt from having looked at her statement, but, in fact, sir, that's not what you said all along and, in fact, I put to you it's been very clear all along that you've only known the location of this street and that's what you've referred to. Let me take you through that just so it's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: If we can look at your testimony from Wednesday which is T-11568.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, if we look at line 16 there you were asked: "From Lapska Street can you see Kojlovica?" Your answer was: "The village of Kojlovica cannot be seen from Lapska Street."

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: If we can scroll down to 11570, line 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Again there the question is whether from the location number 1, which was you circling a large swathe of the street, a person can see the village of Lukare. You say, No, it's not possible, and again you say, "from Lapska Street, you cannot see Lukare." And if you scroll down again to 11572, line 20. Again, sir, "it is impossible. It is impossible," you say. "From Lapska Street, can you not see the Orthodox cemetery." Now, sir, clearly there is a significant difference between different locations that a house may occupy along a long street, but without belabouring that point, let's look, sir, at the specific reason that you gave why it would be impossible to see these places.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: If we can scroll back T-11568, line 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: You were asked there, we just looked at this, but I'll draw your attention to it again. Sorry, actually if we look at line 20, that's easier. You say: "The reason you can't see it is because between Lapska Street and Kojlovica there is no line of sight because of the lie of the land and buildings." So, sir, you are talking about line of sight, lie of the land, and buildings. But, sir, surely there is a significant difference to line of sight or lie of the land or the manner in which buildings might block your view depending where you are on that a long. Do you agree or disagree?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not agree with that. Independently of all of that, can you not see Kojlovica from that place. I said very nicely that there is no optical visibility. Please if necessary can experts go and establish that, I claim that that is impossible and I claim that because I went through that area and I'm convinced of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Very well, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I do have perhaps five to ten minutes left, but I see we are at the time for the second break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will have the second break. This will be a break of an hour, and we would resume at 2.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Behar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, just to finish off with this topic, I'd like to look at one more map. It's a rather simple map.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, this is a very simple map made by using Google maps, and it shows the basic topography and the elevations of the area that you've been discussing and that Ms. Bala discussed. And letter A on that map shows us the rough location of Ms. Bala's house. Now, sir, do you see Kojlovica on that map?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I see my friend is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, now we have a map on the screen, but we don't know who entered things onto the map and by what means and by what standard. It says here that already some markings were made and that, for example, A should be witness Bala's house, but I don't think that is customary. We should have a pristine map. Perhaps the witness can answer, but I don't think it's been our practice so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Fortunately, Mr. Djurdjic, we don't often need to Google. This is a fairly standard form Google map, and even I can see from the indication of main streets of the town, that the circle with A in the middle is in the approximate position of Lapska Street. The town or village names appear to be a standard part of the Google map. So I think accepting that there may be no particular proof of details at the moment, nevertheless this has a sufficient appearance of normality and authenticity to allow the questioning to continue. Please do so, Mr. Behar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And, sir, I can indicate that actually on the map itself we put in the address, you can see it at the top of the screen, of 30 Lapi or Lapska Street, and that's the A that's come up, but would you agree, sir, that the A is the approximate location of Lapska Street; does that seem right to you? I see you're nodding, sir, I take that as a yes? Okay. Sir, just to return to my question, do you see Kojlovica on that map?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness could be provided with a pen to make some markings.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: If you could just circle Kojlovica. Put a number 1 next to that.

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Now, it would seem clear from this map, sir, that Kojlovica is at elevation, correct? In other words, it's up on a hill, in a hilly area?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you tell me what is it that you are asking me precisely?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Well, I'm just asking you, sir, and you can see it from the map, but I'll ask you the question in any event, Kojlovica is at elevation, in other words, it's not at sea level, it is up high on a hill or in a hilly area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not. And we can't see that on this map. Kojlovica, or at least most of it, is in a flat area, and as for the names, you can put it above, slightly under, or to the east, west, north, or south. The name does not necessarily have to be in the same spot where the location is. Just take a look at where it says "Pristina," it's in one place only of the town. Topographic markings are slightly different to locations themselves. They are usually placed next to a location. If we want to have a centre of town marked precisely it has to be marked with a dot. Otherwise on this map we have places at a higher altitude than --

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I think we have your position, and I'm not really concerned about where the letters are on the map, sir. But you can see that that whole area, it appears quite clear, is at elevation as compared to Pristina which is flat. My question for you is, are you saying, sir, that Kojlovica is not at elevation, that general area?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just above Kojlovica on several sides there are hills. Kojlovica itself is not on the same altitude. Another thing that is important and that is in colour on this map is as follows: Between Kojlovica and Pristina and Lapska Street, there are obstacles that are higher than Kojlovica and Pristina themselves. That is very important to note.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: We've covered the issue of obstacles, sir, we don't need to return to that and if you can just stay focused on my questions. Let's look -- I think we have your position there, sir. Let's look at Dragodan. Can you indicate where Dragodan is there on this map? I'm not sure that it's actually marked.

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see it approximately here. That should be it although I'm not positive.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: You agree, sir, that Dragodan is at elevation? In fact --

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of Dragodan is, or at least a part of it, but not all of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: In fact, sir, there's an area called Dragodan hill, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is likely. Dragodan does exist but whether there is an elevation or a hill, I can't tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: In fact, sir, it was Dragodan hill that Ms. Bala referred to. I won't take you there, but I can leave this site, it's T-2289, line 14. Now and how about Vranjevac, sir, can you indicate where that would be on the map? Sorry, actually before I do that, you did just circle an area, Dragodan. The area that you circled, for Dragodan, can you just put a number 2 next to that.

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now I'd asked if you could mark the area that Vranjevac is in, if you could put a circle there and a number 3.

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vranjevac is quite large, and this map is not very good for me to mark it. If you insist, I will, but one cannot establish exactly where Vranjevac is. In terms of area size, Vranjevac is quite large. This map is not very good for that. I marked it on the previous map. I think it should be enough to compare. If you press me into marking it here, that may not be so convenient not because of my lack of knowledge, but because of the type of map this is, and it is not very -- a very good means to mark such an area.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: That's fine, sir. It doesn't need to be pin-point accurate marking, but if you can just indicate the general area that Vranjevac is in on this map. Put a number 3. I won't hold you to it being exactly correct.

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: If you can put a number 3.

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And that is also at elevation, is it not, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not all of it. Part of it is. The rest is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Let me be specific then, sir. Both you and Ms. Bala refer to the Vranjevac hill. I'm presuming that a hill is at elevation and is above the things surrounding it, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, can you indicate Taslixhe on the map. Circle that area broadly and perhaps mark it with a 4. It is actually labelled on the map.

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Again it would appear clear from that map that that area is at elevation just judging from the ridges which indicate elevation, do you agree with that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way it is shown here it appears to be, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And finally, sir, if you could indicate the location of Lukare or Lukare on this map? If you can circle that and put a number 5.

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Would you agree, sir, that Lukare and certainly parts of Lukare are also at elevation?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are not. Lukare is not at elevation.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Well, in fact, sir, Ms. Bala stated that she saw a tank firing from a hill in Lukare. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. Lukare itself has no hills. Further afield there are some though. This road goes through Lukare and the military warehouse is right next to the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Well, sir, if someone is --

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The road between Pristina and Medvedje.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, if something is on a hill, then obviously it's at elevation, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lukare is not at elevation. And the warehouse is not at elevation. It is in a flat area next to the road. Around that, though, there is a number of hills.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Well, let's look then very briefly at what you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: If we can see - this is again from Wednesday's testimony - T-11575.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you wanting anything done with this map?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Oh, yes, sorry. Yes, I would seek to tender the map at this time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received, but we do bear in mind the points made by Mr. Djurdjic in his objection, so don't overlook that reservation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the map will be Exhibit P01542.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And if you look, sir, this is actually in your testimony in chief, in fact, this is how it was put to you when you were asked to describe the Lukare firing and what Ms. Bala said. The question is beginning at line 11, Ms. Bala says on page 2341 of the transcript, line 22 and 23 and 24 and 25 that she saw a tank firing in the village of Lukare firing from a hill there towards the hill of Kojlovica. So just to be clear, there, sir, even as it was put to you, you are talking about hills in that area. Is that consistent with your understanding of the topography?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Now, generally speaking, sir, would you agree that it's easier to see something, certainly something at a distance when it's up on a hill above you?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, provided that between that elevation and the place she says could be seen there are no obstacles. The village of Lukare is not on a hill, do bear that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: You have already told us today, sir, that Lapska Street was in a flat area, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Very well. Now, sir, in a more general respect with respect to your testimony, I've noticed that in a number of respects you've claimed not just that you observe something happened, but that you had a very direct and personal connection to it. So you spoke personally, according to your evidence, to Albanians who told you that they were leaving because of the NATO bombing, correct? You recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: You testified that you looked out your window and saw people moving in fake convoys, you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall looking out my window. If I said so, and I believe there are audio recordings to double-check that, then I guess you are right, but I really don't recall having said that I was looking out my window.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Well, we can look at that, sir, but you did certainly say that you saw personally people moving in these fake convoys, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did say that, and it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: You say that you personally saw and handled depleted uranium projectiles, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said that too.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: You said that you yourself were with General Lazarevic on April 27th and 28th, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said I was with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: As we've just discussed, you say that you personally know that Nazalie Bala could not possibly have seen those observations that she described and that you commented on, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that from Lapska Street Number 30 or from anywhere in Lapska Street, one cannot see the village of Kojlovica, and I repeat that for the umpteenth time, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Very well, sir. I put to you, sir, that in making all of these claims that you've, in fact, specifically tailored your evidence and fabricated your evidence in order to assist the Defence case however possible on each of those specific points. Do you agree, sir, or do you disagree?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why would I specifically tailor anything? I see this as an insult. I declare that I will tell the truth, and this is what I did. And nothing else. I didn't make up anything. I only told you what I saw or heard at the time it happened. End of story.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Those are my questions for you. I know my learned friend may have some follow-up questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Behar. Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, my learned friend insisted repeatedly on the claim that from the Lapska Street you could see Lukare and Kojlovica and you claimed that there's no line of sight. So can you explain to the Trial Chamber why there is no line of sight from Lapska Street to Kojlovica and Lukare?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my answer to your question is very brief. There's no line of sight for several reasons. One of the reasons is because there are obstacles, natural and man-made obstacle between the two. So there is not an optical line of sight, you cannot see you from one to the other. And another reason is, well, despite the fact that it says there that the events were observed from the attic of a house that has five stories, it is indicated that two stories are underground and three are above ground. As far as I know, two plus two makes four, not five, so if you have two stories that are underground, then you can only watch something, observe something from the second floor and not from the fifth floor, but the basic key reason is that there are man made and natural obstacles.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell me, if you were to stand in Lapska Street and there's a straight line from there to the point above Kojlovica, how far is it, what is the distance?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said at the time that it was about 5 kilometres. That's likely the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, from Lapska Street if you look to Lukare in a straight line, what would the distance be there?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it would be more than 3 kilometres, but I can't really tell you. I took that road to Medvedje and Kacikovo, and I went there to a visit the depot more than 3 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You are an officer, a military officer. If you could see something at that distance using a pair of binoculars, could you see an object the size of a tank, see it and recognise it?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't think that you could do that with a fair of ordinary binoculars, but it's not the key thing here. There are man-made and natural obstacles which prevent you from looking and seeing from the point where the person claims was observing to the place where this person claims the tanks were and where fire was opened from and so on, so that is the key thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now, I would like us to look at P1542. It's just been admitted. If we could look at it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, you marked under number 2, Dragodan. Could you tell us where would the cemetery be?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The cemetery is not as high up as Dragodan itself, the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can the witness go on and make some additional markings on this map and then we can perhaps admit is in that form? No?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It can be done as a separate exhibit. It would be perhaps helpful if there was a another colour pen. You may have a blue pen now, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, Colonel. Do you have a blue pen?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have this pen here. I don't know what colour it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, you can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Very well. Could you please mark it 6, with 6. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, let me quote from Ms. Bala's statement at page 2341, lines 12 through 17: "When I looked towards Dragodan from the terrace, I observed the area close to the cemetery, and I could see the police forces moving in armoured personnel carriers, trucks and other vehicles." So if this is A and we know that this A, it's the house in Lapska Street, this new technology is very accurate, what are the obstacles preventing the witness Bala from seeing the cemetery?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Man-made and natural obstacles between Lapska Street, her house in Lapska Street, and the site where the Serbian Orthodox cemetery is located in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, I would like us to look at D50.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you wanting this as an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Of course that's why we made those markings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00719.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, can you see this marking number 1?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is that Lapska Street?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, unfortunately not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, tell me, if we look at where Lapska Street is on this map, can you see the Dragodan cemetery?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not Lapska Street, but that doesn't change anything. You cannot see the Dragodan cemetery either from this location or from where Lapska Street really is. You cannot see the village of Kojlovica either because of those obstacles.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The presiding judge, His Honour Judge Parker asked the witness to circle the railway station, and it's marked with number 4 here. To the best of your knowledge, can you tell us where the railway station actually is, if you can indeed see it on this map?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I have an objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is not the railway station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Behar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is not, in my submission, a proper scope of re-examination. This is something that could have been explored in chief, but this is not anything that arises out of my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think it is in the context of physical obstructions to views, so I would allow Mr. Djurdjic to continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us now where the railway station is. First tell us.

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The location marked with number 4 is not the railway station in Pristina. The railway station is at a different location. It's to the south-west of that location. If you allow me, I will mark the location of the railway station on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But let us first explain that in words. If you go south-west of this circle here, can you read on the map?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can circle the location where the railway station is if you allow me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: With the blue pen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is that the blue pen?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And I think you should mark it with number 5.

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, yes, you can see some buildings here where you made this marking. Is it possible to see the cemetery from Lapska Street given its position?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you cannot see the cemetery because there are natural and man-made obstacles which make it impossible to see anything. And in particular, this location marked with number 4, it's an overpass which is higher than the rest of the structures there, and this is the overpass that Bala used every day as she went to work in Dragodan.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you something about Vranjevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we could please look at D717. I would actually prefer to see D011-2339. And I would like to tender this into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00720.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we could zoom in a little bit from the middle of the page up. Yes. A little bit further up, if you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, can we see now the whole of Vranjevac, or should we scroll down a little bit?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can see most of it, but you could scroll down perhaps a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we then scroll down a little bit. No, no, the other way. Down. A little bit more.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I think that now we can see the whole of Vranjevac?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, I would like to ask you this, and I don't want to lead you here. We can see a railway line which almost bisects this map going north/south. Now, does this railway line skirt Vranjevac?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the railway line that goes from Pristina through Podujevo to Kursumlija and then further down.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Now, please take the pen and can you just mark the borders of Vranjevac. And on the other side, north-west. Do we have it or not?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, could you please place a number 1 next to those borders. Just write number 1 so that we know that this first line that you drew in marks the borders of Vranjevac?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Filipovic, is the whole of Vranjevac located on a hill?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vranjevac is on a hill on the slopes and then it also extends into the plain next to the railway line.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: My question to you is this: You've shown us where the railway line is. Can you tell us approximately where the top of the Vranjevac hill is?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a little bit more to the north.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: More to the north than what we see here?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at the edge.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Of the map that we have here?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at the edge of this map next to the cattle market.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now, from Lapska Street to the top of the hill to the highest elevation, how far is it?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As the crow flies it's more than 2 kilometres, the straight line is more than 2 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I would like to know this: Can you now draw in where Lapska Street is?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That's number 2.

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You mentioned that there was a barracks that was relocated on the eve of the war. Now, the barracks, was it here on the hilly side, or was it beyond the hills on the other side?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The barracks was in the plain there where the Pristina-Kosovo-Polje Road is. So if you leave Pristina and head towards Kosovo Polje, you take what used to be Lenjinova Street, and to the right right next to the Pristina-Kosovo-Polje railway line, that's where the barracks was and that's where it is, in fact, to this day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does it have anything to do with the part of Vranjevac that was attacked?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Topographically speaking, no, no, there's no connection whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Here if you could just mark at the bottom, if you could just mark the Vranjevac overpass.

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it, and I can mark it if you allow me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I marked the Vranjevac overpass, the one that goes over the railway line, and I marked it with number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, from the beginning of the war until the end, did you ever see on that overpass any armoured vehicles or tanks?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no armoured vehicles or tanks there ever and for several reasons and I explained that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you very much. Please just focus on the questions that I'm asking you and answer just to those questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender this map into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be Exhibit D00721.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: My learned friend asked you about the term "Siptar" used for Albanians, and you have given us your explanation. I, myself, call Albanians, Albanians, but I want to know what name did you use for Albanians from the time when you were born until today?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I always called them Siptars because I found that in the textbooks. I was taught by Siptars and that's what they taught me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And were these schools that you attended ethnically mixed?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, my high school had seven classes in the fourth grade; four in Serbian, two in Albanian, and one in Turkish. That was in 1967.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at P869. Or rather, P896, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, this is an order of the command of the military district dated the 27th of March, 1999, and it was shown to you during the cross-examination. I wanted to ask you whether this unit, or rather, these units of the military district had armoured combat vehicles?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not a single one. The formation that was called the military district of Pristina did not have a single one. That can be seen from its book of establishment, and everyone knows that there was no such vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My learned friend said that this order shows that roads were supposed to be secured, so tell us what kind of security was provided along roads by these detachments?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These detachments or rather, these military territorial units carry out in-depth security activities for various roads, buildings, et cetera. It's done in the following way: They will be deployed along a road, and they will be at a certain distance but by their very disposition they will make it impossible for Siptar terrorist forces to attack these roads, et cetera. They had to be deployed in such a way also because of NATO action against roads. If they were to be directly on roads, they would be a direct target.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do they have anything to do with the regulation of traffic on the roads that they secured?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had nothing to do with that at all. And that was not part of their duties either. It was the police units that were in charge of that, and they did that in accordance with regulations. They asked citizens to show IDs and during these ID checks many policemen were killed by Siptar terrorists throughout Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please now have P982. No, 928 actually. Again, I'd like to ask if we could have a map. D011-2339. Could we please zoom in on this little box or square. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you find your way here, can you see or --

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can orient myself for the most part.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in this box we have the town of Pristina marked with the surrounding area.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: From the document that I asked for previously, P928, paragraph 2 was shown to you concerning the 15th Armoured Brigade. So it says --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We do not have the document now in e-court any longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Goles, Obilic, and Gracanica. Could you please underline Obilic, Gracanica, and Goles?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Gracanica, number 1. Obilic, number 2. And Goles, Goles I cannot find it exactly, but it should be roughly in this area. That would be number 3. Number 3, Goles, the map is not very legible, but Goles would be in that area roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So in number 2, in that area, or rather, the broader area of Pristina, that is where forces had to be on the ready for anti-sabotage fighting on this elevation, and you describe these three points to us, that those were the points that were being defended. Could you draw a line in terms of how you understand this broader area of Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The broader area of Pristina would mean outside these features. I will try to explain it by way of a circle, if you allow me to do so. Everything outside this line is the broader area of Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please put number 4 on that circle.

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The broader area is marked with a number 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let us try to make it as clear as possible. In relation to this circle that you drew, where is the broader area?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In relation to the circle, the broader area is outside that circle.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, I'd like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00722.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have P928, and have a look at paragraph 4, and it's page 5 in the English version. It is page 2 in the B/C/S. Could we have the end of the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please read paragraph 4 to yourself, Mr. Filipovic, and could we please have your comments once you've read it?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "In all" --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Not aloud. To yourself.

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you. I have read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please give us your comments? What does paragraph 4 mean?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my view, it is basically clear, namely, that in all garrisons and garrison posts and deployment areas, deployment areas first and foremost, and areas of responsibility in co-ordinated action with MUP forces, the military territorial units and the military investigating and judicial organs, ensure the control of the territory and the functioning of the authorities, prevent looting, theft, and other forms of crime, war profiteering, protect the civilian population from robbery and establish law and order. That was the task, very clear. It is put rather generally, but it is very clear, and that was done throughout the aggression. Of course, along with all the difficulties caused by the activity of Siptar terrorists and the NATO air force.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tell me, are there any combat activities in these actions that are ordered in paragraph 4?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there are just tasks that are spelled out in general terms. In order to control the territory, ensure the functioning of the system of government, protection of the civilian population, and that is what the MUP did together with military units in a dignified and honourable manner throughout the aggression.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have page 3 now in the Serbian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please read the first paragraph on page 3 to yourself.

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I have read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. First of all, what are garrisons and garrison posts?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In accordance with the rules of service of the Army of Yugoslavia, there were garrisons and garrison posts, and that is what the regulations said, that there was this classification. Now, on the basis of this, we can see that the military police were supposed to be of involved as well. I omitted to say a few moments ago that for checking roads and securing roads, in addition to the police units carrying out checks there was also the military police who have their own line of work. So they co-operated there in that field, and they provided for unhindered traffic and checks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: One more question. You were the temporary commander of the Pristina garrison during the war. I would be interested in one particular thing. The area of responsibility of a unit is one thing, I'm referring to the brigade, and the place where it is is a different matter. In every brigade was there also a company of the military police?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In units at brigade level as far as I can remember at regimental level as well there were military police units that had their specific tasks especially in this period of aggression. They had the task of providing law and order and checking traffic, providing security for the commander, and the forward command post and carrying out other tasks in accordance with the rules of service and the military police. Also they were supposed to safe-guard scenes of crime, they were supposed to be involved in investigations of crimes and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. With regard to these tasks and the military police units as such, did they carry out any kind of combat tasks?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, as far as I know, they were not engaged in any kind of combat tasks. Only the tasks that I referred to. They did that every day and in that area there was no abuse whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your own garrison, during the course of the war in Pristina, did the military police carry out these functions that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military police carried out these functions and that primarily pertains to the 52nd Battalion of the military police that was deployed in the broader area outside the central part of the town of Pristina, and they carried out these tasks and also this was done by the 15th Brigade, the 243rd, and other units who are our neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
